newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-HUNGARY T-BILL YIELDS SEEN LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-HUNGARY T-BILL YIELDS SEEN LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: Hungarian government securities' yields are expected to be steady or a shade firmer at this week's auctions, looking forward to receiving fresh impetus from the July CPI figures to be released next Monday.
"The information that can move the market will be inflation figures to be published next Monday," said Gabor Szogi of Creditanstalt Securities.
Analysts expected the market of government papers of less than one-year maturity remain very stable in coming weeks as well.
"I expect a few basis point rise in August, unless CPI firms a little in July, as expected by analysts," said Tamas Puskas of Raiffeisen Securities.
Yields could go substantially lower in the second half of September, depending on macroeconomic developments and once investors are back from holidays, he said.
Analysts said the fact that investors, mainly foreigners, were net sellers in long-term government papers, left the market virtually intact.
"Yields of papers with maturity of less than one year are very stable," Puskas said. "The fact that everybody is net seller in long-term papers has hardly any impact."
Puskas said the market absorbed the state's supply of government papers at lower prices and higher yields, reflecting lack of interest in summer doldrums.

This happened at the auction of three-year series 2000/F bond last Thursday as the bond's average annual yield soared to 17.75 percent from 17.14 percent at an auction a week before, while the maximum jumped to 17.82 percent from 17.33.
